analysis.analysis: The kenotic reading presented through established literary venues. 'The "kenotic truth" of Sappho refers to an interpretation of her poetry — most famously Fragment 31 — that focuses on kenosis (a Greek term meaning "emptying out"). In this reading, the speaker experiences a radical self-emptying or ego-death through the overwhelming, embodied intensity of romantic longing' (www.openhorizons... +4). Expanded: The Kenosis in Fragment 31 — 'love is frequently not just a joyful emotion but an all-consuming force that strips the speaker of their composure' (www.openhorizons... +1); Self-Annihilation — 'the speaker observes a man sitting opposite her beloved. As she watches her beloved laugh, she is "emptied" of her own voice, sight, and coherent thought' (The Paris Review). SciLynk organic: 'The Kenotic Truth of Sappho 31: A Document for the Liberation...'
